name: Stratum Mid-Grade Pressed Occasion Set
description: The Tier 3 worker's best effort, worn to presentations, performance reviews, and the occasional internal ceremony they were not expecting to attend. The Stratum Mid-Grade Pressed Occasion Set is a two-piece suit in medium charcoal poly-blend — not cheap enough to be embarrassing, not fine enough to be mistaken for something better. The jacket has a notched lapel of moderate width, single-breasted, two-button, and fits well enough off the rack if the wearer is within standard sizing brackets. The lining is a thin acetate in pale grey that makes a faint rustling sound when the arms move — a telltale that only the wearer notices but cannot stop noticing. Underneath, a white Stratum broadcloth shirt with a point collar, the placket ever so slightly puckered from repeated ironing. A synthetic-silk tie in deep burgundy sits knotted in a four-in-hand, slightly asymmetric in the way of all self-tied ties. Trousers are flat-front in matching charcoal poly-blend, pressed with a center crease the wearer set themselves the night before, one crease slightly off-center in a way that will bother them all day. Footwear is a pair of Stratum-brand matte-black derby shoes, adequate in construction, resoled once at a street cobbler. The entire ensemble was purchased at a Stratum corporate outlet and comes with a two-year 'professional appearance guarantee,' which is a warranty no one has ever successfully claimed. Gene-incompatible by default — the cut assumes a fully standard humanoid silhouette and accommodates nothing else.
functionality: Stain-resist finish on jacket exterior, machine-washable shirt, wrinkle-recovery trouser fabric rated for moderate commute, standard RFID badge clip loop at breast pocket
what_it_says: This is someone who cares about being taken seriously but does not yet have the resources to guarantee it. Every element of this outfit is correct in category but slightly off in execution — the puckered placket, the off-center crease, the asymmetric tie — and those micro-imperfections are a map of what the wearer did themselves versus what they could afford to have done for them. It is the outfit of aspiration worn at the edge of its means, and everyone above Tier 3 can read it instantly.
worn_by: Tier 3 office workers at internal presentations
cubicle staff attending promotion review boards
junior clerks assigned to client-facing meetings without warning
Tier 3 workers attending corponation internal ceremonies
anyone who owns exactly one suit
manufacturer: Stratum Corporate Services Apparel — Standard Occasions Line
story_hooks: The wearer is called into a Tier 5 boardroom without notice and has to walk in wearing this — the contrast between their suit and every other suit in the room is a kind of violence, and the Tier 5 executives use it.

Someone finds a dry-cleaning receipt in the jacket's breast pocket from three years ago with a name on it — the suit was purchased secondhand, and the original owner is a person who has since gone missing under circumstances the corponation has officially resolved.

A Tier 4 character recognizes this exact suit because they wore one for four years before their promotion — the sight of it on someone else triggers a moment of sharp, uncomfortable memory about what it felt like to care this much about a single crease.
